Schema payoff is measurable: <cite index="15-10,15-11">pages with FAQ schema are reported 2.8x more likely to be cited in AI answers, and the core stack for a local service business is LocalBusiness + Service + Review + FAQPage + Organization</cite> (https://evolveamz.com/local-business-ai-search-guide/).

Success at 60 days = NEMO named or cited in 3 of 10 manual test prompts ('who installs half round copper gutters in York PA', 'gutter guard cost York County') across Claude and Perplexity, and the AI-answer-engine visitor count off zero for the first time.

techniques.name: Six real York County authority links (chamber, suppliers, historic groups)
techniques.hypothesis: The site's ranking problem is prominence, not pages: it already sits top-3 for almost nothing across 87 tracked queries while thin national aggregators outrank it. A handful of genuinely local, hand-vetted links — York County Economic Alliance / local chamber membership, the coil and brake supplier's 'installers we sell to' page, a HARB-adjacent or historic-district preservation resource list where copper and half-round matter, a local realtor or home-inspector site — do double duty: they are the prominence signal Google cross-checks, and they are also the third-party mentions AI engines read as credibility for York specifically. Better still, several of these audiences are humans who refer work: chamber directories and historic-district resource pages put Eric in front of people who own 1890s brick rowhouses with rotting half-round, which is the highest-ticket work he does.
techniques.evidence: <cite index="25-1,25-2">Links from locally relevant sites — other businesses in the market, local news, chamber of commerce, community organisations — carry disproportionate weight for local organic and map-pack rankings, and a single chamber link is worth more than dozens of generic national links</cite> (https://www.searchscaleai.com/blog/local-seo-guide-rank-google-maps-2026/). Practitioners report the same from the field: <cite index="26-1,26-2,26-3,26-4">better results from one chamber-of-commerce backlink than from dozens of random directories, with citation cleanup rarely moving the needle</cite> (https://www.fitzdesignz.com/blog/local-seo-in-action-how-2026-ranking-factors-compare-to-what-we-see-on-the-ground). Roofing-specific guidance agrees that <cite index="24-1,24-2,24-3">links from a supplier, local news story, chamber, or manufacturer certification page signal real-world prominence, and a handful of genuine local links beats any volume of low-quality directory links</cite> (https://cleartrailsolutions.com/local-seo-for-roofers/). On the AI side, <cite index="15-8">a chamber of commerce listing is argued to carry more AI weight than 20 generic directory listings combined</cite> (https://evolveamz.com/local-business-ai-search-guide/).
techniques.notes:
first step: Price and apply for the local chamber / York County Economic Alliance membership tier that includes a linked directory listing, and in the same sitting email the aluminium coil supplier asking to be added to their 'find an installer' page — an honest ask with no payment involved.
effort: weeks
cost: under $100/mo
expected: 6 earned links from York-County-rooted domains in 90 days (target list of 15, ~40% yield). Leading indicator: the tracked top-3 share moving off 2.3% on town-plus-service queries within 60–90 days of the first links landing; lagging indicator: 1–2 phone calls that name the chamber directory or a historic-district referral.

techniques.name: Missed-call text-back on the business line
techniques.hypothesis: The AI agent catches calls it answers, but it cannot catch the caller who hangs up at ring 3, calls at 8pm, or gets a busy signal while Eric is talking to someone else — and those are exactly the homeowners with water running down a wall. An automatic SMS back to the number that just called ('Sorry I missed you — I'm on a roof in York. What's the address and what's the gutter doing? I can text you a range today.') keeps the conversation alive in the 8-minute window before they dial the next gutter company. With only 300 profile views and ~6 visits a day, NEMO cannot afford to leak a single inbound call; this is the only lever that adds booked estimates without adding a single visitor.
techniques.evidence: 2026 home-services write-ups put missed-call text-back at the top of the automation list for owner-operators: <cite index="25-9,25-10,25-11">most service businesses miss 30 to 60 percent of inbound calls, most of those callers book the next available competitor within about 8 minutes, and the text-back closes that window</cite> (https://netpartners.marketing/missed-call-text-back-highest-roi-automation-service-businesses/). Reply rates are high because the caller initiated contact: <cite index="28-2,28-3">SMS reply rates from missed-call text-back average 35 to 50 percent for home service businesses versus 5 to 10 percent for cold outbound SMS, because the caller already wanted to reach you</cite> (https://www.marqeable.com/blog/missed-call-text-back-home-services/). Speed is the whole game: <cite index="14-12,14-13">CallRail's 2026 home services research found responding within 60 seconds lifts conversion 391%, and waiting 5 minutes cuts qualifying odds by 80%</cite> (https://pipelineon.com/blog/contractor-website-conversion-rate/).
techniques.notes:
first step: Turn on missed-call auto-text in the existing phone/AI-agent provider (or a $15-30/mo add-on), with the first message written in Eric's own words, an explicit 'Reply STOP to opt out', and A2P 10DLC brand registration submitted the same day so the carriers do not filter it. Reply-only to inbound callers — never a list, never a blast.
effort: hours
cost: under $100/mo
expected: Text fires on 100% of unanswered/abandoned calls within 60 seconds; 35-50% of those callers reply; over a 60-day test, 3-6 conversations that would otherwise have been silence, and 1-2 booked estimates that show up in the ledger as 'recovered missed call'.

techniques.name: Heavy-rain 48-hour response play (overflow page + GBP post)
techniques.hypothesis: York County gets thunderstorm bands in August and nor'easter rain in September, and the moment a gutter overflows over the front door a homeowner searches 'gutters overflowing in heavy rain' or 'gutter pulling away from house' — that is a next-7-days job, not a next-spring job. NEMO has no page owning that emergency wording and posts nothing when it rains. One permanent diagnostic page ('Why your gutters overflow in heavy rain — and what it costs to fix in York County'), phone-first, plus a Business Profile post pushed within hours of a National Weather Service heavy-rain or wind advisory for York County, puts the business in front of demand that is already compressed into 48 hours and that no local gutter contractor is timing for. IndexNow is already wired, so the page can be re-pushed the same morning.
techniques.evidence: Weather is a targeting signal, not backdrop: <cite index="36-2,36-3">a heat wave, early frost, or storm front creates a predictable spike in demand, and brands that plan around those triggers convert at a different rate than always-on generic activity</cite> (https://kortx.io/news/home-services-marketing-playbook/). The window is short and the first responder wins: <cite index="39-1">demand compresses instantly, repairs are non-optional, and homeowners typically contact 2-3 contractors within the first 24-48 hours and decide within 72</cite> (https://www.pinkcallers.com/blog/how-storm-season-creates-lead-surges-for-contractors). Rain-driven query surges are documented in the adjacent trade: <cite index="37-16">'roof leak repair' (+69%) and 'emergency roof repair' (+70%) show consistent seasonal surges driven by heavy rain or storm activity</cite> (https://stacker.com/stories/small-business/seasonal-search-shifts-home-services-demand-what-spikes-when-and-how-stay). And <cite index="40-23,40-24,40-25">contractors who build the landing page and response system 60-90 days before storm season capture far more of it than those who scramble after</cite> (https://resultcalls.com/blog/how-to-use-seasonal-roofing-marketing-to-get-roofing-leads) — which is exactly what August 1 is, 60 days ahead of PA leaf-fall and the autumn rain.
techniques.notes:
first step: Write the overflow diagnostic page today: symptom-first headings (water sheeting over the front, gutter sagging at the seam, downspout backing up), an honest 'what this usually costs in York County' band, Eric's number as the first thing under the fold, and photos of real York jobs. Then subscribe the phone to NWS alerts for York County zone PAZ066 so the trigger is automatic, not remembered.
effort: days
cost: free
expected: One page live before Labor Day; a GBP post inside 12 hours of every NWS heavy-rain/wind advisory for York County (roughly 6-10 events between now and December). Success = the overflow page becomes a top-5 landing page by October and produces 2+ calls per rain event week, plus measurable GBP 'call' actions clustered on advisory days.

techniques.name: Apple Business + Bing Places verified place cards
techniques.hypothesis: The ledger's AI-answer work is all on-site — it assumes the engines can read nemoseamlessgutter.com. But when a York homeowner asks Siri or Copilot 'who installs gutters near me', those assistants do not read the site first, they read the place-card graph. NEMO is invisible there. Two free verified listings (Apple, Bing) with the exact same name/address/phone as the GBP put the business into the two datasets that Siri, Copilot and ChatGPT search lean on for local trade queries, and they double as high-authority citations that raise the map-pack prominence the site is currently short of. This is an afternoon of work that cannot be undone by an algorithm update, and it is the cheapest fix available for the '0 AI answer engine visitors' line.

Setup is trivial and free: <cite index="22-21,22-24,22-25">fifteen minutes of setup buys a permanent accurate presence in the data source AI assistants check first, and claiming and verifying costs nothing</cite> (https://osprey.solutions/blog/bing-places-for-business-2026). On the Apple side, <cite index="21-1,21-2">Apple Business Connect is one of a small number of trusted nodes AI systems verify a business against, so investment there improves local AI visibility beyond iOS</cite> (https://www.trymaas.com/blog/apple-business-connect-apple-maps-marketers-2026/), and <cite index="23-19,23-20,23-21">Siri increasingly names one or two specific businesses conversationally rather than listing links — if the business is not in Apple's data pipeline it will never be named</cite> (https://www.marketingcode.com/apple-intelligence-siri-contractors-invisible/). first step: Claim the Apple place card at businessconnect.apple.com using the exact GBP name, address, phone and hours, and upload the same 8-10 real job photos already on the GBP — then do Bing Places the same afternoon, and report any duplicate listings found on either.
effort: hours
cost: free

Baseline test: ask Siri, Copilot and ChatGPT 'seamless gutter installer in York PA' before and 30 days after — target going from 0/3 naming NEMO to at least 1/3. techniques.name: Trade-partner referral loop (roofers, siders, painters)
techniques.hypothesis: Every roof replacement and siding job in York County ends with gutters off the house and someone has to hang them back. Roofing crews in York, Dover and Red Lion mostly sub that work out or fumble it. Eric is a one-truck operator with a brake — he can be the guy a roofer calls the same week, and those calls arrive pre-sold with no ad spend and no ranking required. This is the fastest path from 0 phone-agent leads to a ringing phone that does not depend on fixing the map pack first, and it front-loads work before leaf season.
techniques.evidence: A 2026 gutter-specific lead-gen breakdown argues referral partnerships are a core channel and that <cite index="20-3,20-4">a single relationship with a local roofing contractor can produce substantial annual gutter revenue at no advertising cost (https://resultsdigitalus.com/how-gutter-company-lead-generation-works-in-2026/). General contractor guidance says the same: when a roofer replaces a roof the homeowner often needs gutters or siding, and these cross-referrals cost nothing and come with a built-in recommendation (https://projul.com/blog/how-to-get-more-construction-leads/), and a gutter-focused referral piece points at roofers, metal roofers, painters and landscapers as the trades that see gutter problems first (https://www.talentsintoprofits.com/how-to-get-more-referrals).

first step: Build a list of 10 York County roofing/siding/exterior-painting companies that are NOT gutter installers (check their GBP service list to confirm), then call or stop by the first three this week with one sentence: 'I hang seamless gutter same-week for your crews, I invoice you or the homeowner, and I'll send you every roof and siding lead I run into.'
effort: days
cost: free
expected: 8 partner conversations in 3 weeks; 3 that send at least one job; 2-4 referred estimates a month by October, at higher close rate than web leads because they arrive warm. Track as a named lead source in the ledger.

techniques.name: Leaf-season callback to past customers and unsold estimates
techniques.hypothesis: Eric already has a small list of people who bought from him and a larger one who got a quote and never called back. In York County the fall leaf-fall window is when a homeowner will finally say yes to cleaning, guards or the replacement they deferred in spring — and early August is exactly when to book that calendar, before the phone starts ringing on its own in October. This targets booked estimates directly, not traffic, and it is the only channel here where the prospect already knows Eric's name. Outreach is to people with a prior business relationship only — a personal call or a personal email, never a bulk blast.

The same firm names gutter cleaning in October as the season-relevant offer for this trade (https://prestyj.com/blog/home-services-off-season-revenue-customer-database-2026), and a 2026 email/SMS piece recommends one reactivation message, one post-job follow-up and one seasonal reminder as the whole system for a small operator (https://6thman-marketing.com/blog/email-sms-marketing-home-service/).
techniques.notes:
first step: Spend one hour tonight writing out every past customer and every quoted-but-not-sold homeowner from the last two years into a single spreadsheet with name, phone, town, and what was quoted — then call the five oldest quotes tomorrow morning with 'I'm booking the leaf-season calendar now, do you want me on it?'
effort: hours
cost: free
expected: Every past customer and every unsold quote from the last 24 months contacted once by 2026-09-05. Target 10% booking on past customers and 5% on old quotes; even a 40-name list should produce 3-5 booked estimates and fill September.

techniques.name: Answer recommendation threads in York County Facebook groups
techniques.hypothesis: 'Anyone know a good gutter guy?' gets posted in York, Dover, Dallastown and Red Lion township Facebook groups every single week, and each of those posts is a homeowner buying within 30 days — the exact person the map pack is currently failing to deliver. Eric answering in his own name, with a photo of a job on a street the group recognises, converts far better than a rank-3 organic listing and needs no budget. It also seeds third-party mentions of the business name, which is the prominence signal the site is short on.

A 2026 lead-source roundup makes the same point that community group participation, not broadcast posting, is where contractors get traction on Facebook (https://www.builderleadconverter.com/blog/how-to-get-more-construction-leads/).
techniques.notes:
first step: Join the six largest York County / township community Facebook groups today, read each group's pinned rules for what they allow from business owners, and set a 10-minute daily habit of searching the word 'gutter' in each group and replying only to threads asking for a recommendation.
effort: hours
cost: free
expected: Membership in 6-8 York County groups within a week; 3-5 genuine recommendation-thread replies a week; 2-4 inbound calls a month by October, plus organic tags from past customers.

techniques.name: Reply to all 13 reviews, publicly fix the low ones
techniques.hypothesis: 300 GBP views a month produce zero calls, and the profile shows 4.2 stars with 13 reviews and (almost certainly) no owner replies. A York homeowner comparing three gutter installers on Maps sees a 4.2 next to competitors' 4.8s and taps the other guy. Eric cannot delete a bad review, but a specific, non-defensive reply under each one — what happened, what he did about it, and a real offer to make it right — changes the story a reader sees in the two seconds before they decide to call. Replies also add indexable service+town text to the profile ('re-hung the front run in Dallastown') without keyword stuffing, and response rate is a controllable ranking input while review count catches up.
techniques.evidence: Whitespark's 2026 Local Search Ranking Factors puts review signals at ~20% of local pack influence, and one 2026 analysis reports that responding to 80%+ of reviews correlates with stronger local pack presence and conversion lifts around 16% (https://searchxpro.com/the-role-of-reviews-in-local-seo-2026-guide). A 5,000-business study found profiles replying to 75%+ of reviews averaged 2.3 positions higher in the local pack (https://flen.in/blog/does-responding-to-google-reviews-help-seo). Rating also gates clicks: 4.0+ profiles reportedly get 92% more clicks than sub-3.0 (https://rankcontractors.com/blog/contractor-google-maps-ranking-guide), and top-ranked local businesses cluster at 4.8–4.9 (https://wisernotify.com/blog/google-review-statistics/), which is the gap NEMO has to close.
techniques.notes:
first step: Tonight, open the GBP reviews tab, sort oldest-first, and write a 40–60 word reply to every review that has none — naming the actual service and town in each ('the half-round on your Springettsbury porch'), and for the negative ones state plainly what went wrong and invite the customer to call Eric's number directly. No canned text, no asking anyone to change a star.
effort: hours
cost: free
expected: 13/13 reviews answered within one evening; response rate 100% and publicly visible. Watch GBP calls and 'website clicks' per 100 profile views for 30 days — moving from 0 calls to 3–6 calls per month on the same ~300 views is the win. Secondary: if a 1-star reviewer amends or updates after a genuine fix, rating moves from 4.2 toward 4.4+.

techniques.name: One real job page per completed install, photographed and dated
techniques.hypothesis: The site has town pages and guides but zero proof — and for a one-truck contractor with 13 reviews, proof is the thing that makes a stranger dial instead of bounce. Publishing a short page per finished job (town, street-level neighborhood, house type, footage, material, guard type, what the problem was, price band, 3–5 of Eric's own photos, date) does three jobs at once: it gives every town page something real and non-duplicative to link to, it creates the specific evidence AI answer engines quote when someone asks 'who does copper half-round gutters near York PA', and it feeds long-tail queries no competitor covers ('copper half-round gutter Dover PA 1890s farmhouse'). It also directly counters the 4.2 rating — a homeowner who can see eleven finished York County jobs with dates forgives a two-year-old bad review.
techniques.evidence: 2026 contractor SEO guidance is converging on packaged job proof rather than blog filler: project pages with the problem, solution, result and a local angle, linked back to the service page, are described as the content that both ranks and gives a nervous homeowner reason to call (https://constructomarketing.com/local-seo-for-contractors/). Original job photos are called out as what proves real field experience versus stock imagery (https://www.altavistasp.com/2026-contractor-seo-checklist/), and for service-area businesses with no storefront the recommendation is real project evidence per town rather than fake addresses (https://hearback.app/blog/local-seo-for-contractors).
techniques.notes:
first step: On the next finished job, before packing the ladder, shoot four photos — the old gutter, the brake forming the run, the finished run from the ground, and the downspout discharge — then write six sentences and publish it as /jobs/<town>-<month-year>-<service>, linked from that town's page.
effort: days
cost: free
expected: 8–12 job pages live by 30 September (one per finished job, ~20 minutes each on the tailgate). Each indexed within 48h via the existing IndexNow push. Target: town pages gain 1–3 real internal links each, and by mid-October at least 5 tracked long-tail queries (material + town) sit in the top 3, plus first non-zero AI-answer-engine referrals.

techniques.name: Claim Yelp page, switch on Request a Quote, answer inside the hour
techniques.hypothesis: This is the one channel that hands Eric a named York County homeowner with a stated gutter problem for zero dollars, rather than hoping a ranking becomes a call. Yelp quote requests cost nothing to receive or answer; the requester has already decided to hire someone this month. Yelp also displays response time publicly, which is a lever a one-man shop with an AI phone agent can actually win — the four competitors who got the same request are, statistically, slow. Bonus: the claimed Yelp page is a NAP-consistent citation that feeds Apple Maps, Bing and the AI assistants, so it works even on days nobody requests a quote.

Yelp publishes response time on the profile and reports businesses replying within a day get roughly 4x more quote requests; lead qualification odds drop about 21x when response slips from 5 to 30 minutes, and ~8 in 10 home-service companies still miss the 5-minute window (https://www.leadwinner.ai/blog/speed-to-lead-statistics/).
techniques.notes:
first step: Claim the existing/unclaimed Yelp listing at biz.yelp.com with the exact same name, phone and service area as the Google profile, enable Request a Quote, and install the Yelp app on Eric's phone with push notifications on so a request buzzes him on the roof.
effort: hours
cost: free
expected: Page claimed and RAQ live this week; public response time under 1 hour within 30 days. Realistic for a York gutter category: 2–5 quote requests a month rising through leaf season, 1–2 converting to a booked estimate — which would double all-time bookings.

techniques.name: Published flat-price fall gutter cleaning as the front door
techniques.hypothesis: Nobody calls a stranger to spend $2,400 on seamless gutter, but plenty of York County homeowners will call in August-October to get gutters cleaned before leaf-fall. Eric already does cleaning. A cleaning job is a 45-minute ladder visit that ends with him standing at the fascia of a house with rusted-out K-style, sagging pitch or no guards — i.e. a warm, in-person installation quote with zero lead cost. The reason the phone is silent is that both the site and the profile only ask for the big-ticket, high-commitment action ('book an estimate'). A named price on a small job is the lowest-friction phone call this business can offer, and it is seasonally perfect right now: August is when PA homeowners book fall cleaning.
techniques.evidence: 2026 contractor conversion data says hiding price loses the visitor and that specific priced offers beat generic copy: a ServiceTitan finding that 73% of customers cite clear upfront pricing as a primary reason for choosing a home-service provider, and advice to publish lines like 'service calls from $99' (https://gohighpointdigital.com/guide/what-every-contractor-website-needs-to-convert-visitors-into-calls/). Ad-copy testing shows offer-plus-price creative converting roughly twice as well as generic creative on the same auction (https://pipelineon.com/blog/google-ads-call-only-campaign-contractor/). Median contractor sites convert 2-4% of visits; the top decile hits 8-12% on the same traffic by fixing offer, call placement and response time, not design (https://pipelineon.com/blog/contractor-website-conversion-rate/).
techniques.notes:
first step: Eric writes down his actual 2026 cleaning prices for three house sizes on paper today, and those exact numbers go live as a headline on the cleaning page with a tap-to-call button above the fold — no ranges he would not honour.
effort: days
cost: free
expected: A real published price band (e.g. ranch under 2,000 sq ft $X, two-storey $Y, add $Z for guards removal) on a /gutter-cleaning-york-pa page, in GBP Services, and in one GBP offer post. Target: 6-10 cleaning calls in the first 30 days from 300 profile views + 200 site visits, 3-4 booked cleans, and at least 1 installation or guard quote written off a cleaning visit by 15 October.

techniques.name: Mystery-call the AI phone agent and add a live human escape hatch
techniques.hypothesis: 300 profile views a month and zero phone-agent leads is not a demand problem, it is a suspicion that the answered-call experience is leaking. The ledger already plans a 5-minute callback on captured leads and a text-back on missed calls, but nothing checks what a York homeowner actually hears at ring one. If the agent sounds robotic, asks too many questions before it gives a human path, or cannot say a price range, the caller hangs up and dials the next gutter guy — and that hang-up never appears in the lead count, so it looks like 'no calls'. There is also a new reason this matters: Google's agentic calling for home repairs means an AI may soon call on the homeowner's behalf, and a call that stalls gets dropped for the next contractor on the list.
techniques.evidence: Around 80% of callers will not leave a voicemail — they hang up and call the next contractor in the results (https://contractortoolstack.com/guides/ai-call-answering-contractors-guide/); Invoca-based figures put small-business missed-call rates near 25% with under 3% leaving a message (https://heyitsclara.com/us/blog/best-ai-phone-answering-service-us-contractors/). Guidance for contractor answering setups stresses natural voice, urgency detection and live transfer with a spoken briefing rather than pure message-taking (https://www.tryyapper.com/resources/best-answering-service-contractors). On Google's July 2026 agentic calling rollout for home repairs: if the phone is answered by voicemail or a slow script, the AI moves to the next contractor (https://www.marketingcode.com/mobile-ai-google-agentic-calling-home-repairs-ai-to-ai-booking-jul-2026/).
techniques.notes:
first step: Today, call the business number from a borrowed phone as a homeowner with an overflowing gutter over the front door and write down verbatim what the agent says in the first 20 seconds.
effort: hours
cost: free
expected: Five mystery calls from numbers Eric does not own — 7:40am, midday, 5:30pm, 8:15pm, Saturday morning — each scored on: seconds to first human-sounding sentence, whether a price range is given, whether 'can I talk to Eric' produces a transfer or a promised callback time. Success = a live-transfer or 'Eric will call you in 5 minutes' path added within a week, and phone-agent leads moving from 0 to at least 4-6 a month at the same traffic, plus GBP Performance call counts pulled to confirm whether calls are arriving at all.

techniques.name: Coordinate-grid map-pack check across York County
techniques.hypothesis: Search Console now measures organic position, but it cannot see the map pack — and the map pack is where 'gutter installer near me' money lands. For a service-area business, rank collapses with distance from the pin, so 'we rank nowhere' and 'we rank fine within two miles of the shop and vanish in Hanover and Red Lion' need completely different responses. A grid check tells Eric whether the town pages, door hangers, review asks and trade-partner outreach already in the ledger should be aimed at Dover and Spring Grove or concentrated in York City. Cheap, one-time-then-monthly, and it stops the biggest ledger items from being spent in the wrong postcode.
